posts.title: Refrigerator Warm but Freezer Cold? What to Check First
posts.seoTitle: Refrigerator Warm but Freezer Cold? | Austin Repair Guide
posts.metaDescription: Learn why a refrigerator can run warm while the freezer stays cold, what you can safely check, and when to schedule refrigerator repair in Austin.
posts.excerpt: A cold freezer and warm fresh-food compartment often point to an airflow or defrost problem. Start with these safe checks.
posts.author: Nova Refrigeration & Appliance Repair
posts.imageAlt: Open refrigerator and freezer compartments in a modern kitchen

sections.heading: Why the two compartments can behave differently
paragraphs: Most refrigerator-freezer combinations cool the freezer first and move some of that cold air into the fresh-food compartment. If airflow is blocked or the circulation fan stops, the freezer may still seem cold while milk and produce begin warming up. A defrost fault can also allow ice to build around the evaporator and restrict the air path.
This symptom does not identify one failed part by itself. Door seals, a blocked vent, fan operation, temperature controls, and frost patterns all matter when narrowing down the cause.

sections.heading: Safe checks you can make at home
paragraphs: Check that food packages are not covering the air vents between compartments. Make sure the doors close fully and the gaskets are clean and seated. If you have a thermometer, check the actual temperatures rather than judging by touch: the refrigerator should stay at 40°F or below and the freezer at 0°F or below.

Look for a thick layer of frost on the freezer's rear interior panel. That can be a clue that the defrost system or airflow needs attention. Note any unusual fan noise and whether the compressor seems to run continuously. Keep the doors closed as much as possible while you decide what to do next.

sections.heading: When to schedule a repair
paragraphs: If the fresh-food compartment remains above a safe temperature after vents and doors are checked, move perishable food to another refrigerator or cooler and arrange a diagnosis. Avoid removing panels or testing live electrical components yourself. A technician can inspect fan operation, the defrost circuit, sensors, and controls in a safe sequence.

Nova repairs refrigerator cooling and airflow problems across Austin and nearby areas. When you call, share the model number, measured temperatures, frost pattern, and any error code. Those details help the technician prepare for the visit.

faq.question: Can an overfilled freezer make the refrigerator warm?
faq.answer: Yes. Food packed tightly against an air vent can restrict circulation. Clear the vents and allow time for temperatures to stabilize, then check with a thermometer.

faq.question: Should I unplug a refrigerator with heavy frost?
faq.answer: A full thaw can temporarily restore airflow, but it does not repair the underlying fault. Protect your food first and arrange a diagnosis if frost returns.

sources.label: FDA: Refrigerator Thermometers — Cold Facts about Food Safety

posts.title: Repair or Replace an Appliance? A Practical Decision Guide
posts.seoTitle: Repair or Replace an Appliance? | Nova Austin Guide
posts.metaDescription: Compare repair cost, appliance age, parts availability, and recurring problems before deciding whether to repair or replace a household appliance.
posts.excerpt: A clear diagnosis and written estimate make the repair-versus-replace decision much easier.
posts.author: Nova Refrigeration & Appliance Repair
posts.imageAlt: Technician inspecting a household washing machine in a bright laundry room

sections.heading: Start with the diagnosis, not a guess
paragraphs: A machine that will not start might need a small switch, a control board, or something unrelated to the appliance, such as the power supply. The same outward symptom can lead to very different repair costs. Ask for a diagnosis and an estimate before deciding to replace a refrigerator, washer, dryer, dishwasher, or oven.

A useful estimate separates labor and parts, explains what failed, and states what is covered if the same problem returns. Compare that with the installed price of a replacement, including delivery, removal, and any cabinet or connection changes.

sections.heading: Consider age, condition, and parts
paragraphs: Age matters, but it should not be the only deciding factor. Look at the appliance's overall condition, how often it has needed service, whether parts are available, and whether the repair addresses the root cause. A well-maintained appliance with a single failed component may be a good repair candidate; a machine with several recurring faults deserves a closer cost comparison.

Built-in and specialty appliances can have a higher replacement cost and may require installation work. In those cases, a repair that initially sounds expensive may still be reasonable when compared with the full cost of replacing the unit.

sections.heading: Make the choice with real numbers
paragraphs: Get the total repair estimate and the realistic all-in replacement price. Consider the warranty on both options and the time needed to complete the work. If the repair is uncertain, ask the technician what additional faults could be found and whether those would change the recommendation.
Nova provides a diagnosis and an up-front estimate before work begins. If repair is impractical, we will explain why so you can make the decision with the facts in front of you.

faq.question: Is an older appliance always worth replacing?
faq.answer: No. Condition, fault, part availability, and replacement cost matter more than age alone. A diagnosis gives you a useful basis for comparison.

faq.question: What should a repair estimate include?
faq.answer: Ask for the diagnosed fault, parts, labor, total price, expected completion time, and any warranty that applies to the repair.

posts.title: Washer Not Draining? Safe Checks Before a Repair
posts.seoTitle: Washer Not Draining? Austin Troubleshooting Guide
posts.metaDescription: Washer full of water after a cycle? Check settings, hose and model-specific filter guidance before scheduling washer repair in Austin.
posts.excerpt: Standing water can come from a cycle setting, a blocked drain path or a failed pump. Use these safe checks to narrow the problem.
posts.imageAlt: Technician inspecting the drain area of a front-load washer

sections.heading: First separate drainage from spin problems
paragraphs: A washer may leave clothes wet because it did not drain, because it did not spin, or because the selected cycle uses a slower spin. Check whether there is standing water in the drum. If the tub is empty but clothes are soaked, tell the technician whether the spin cycle begins, pauses, or shows an error code.

Do not assume the pump has failed based on one load. An unbalanced bulky item, a low-spin setting or excess detergent can also interrupt the expected cycle. Try a model-approved drain or spin cycle only if there is no leak or unusual noise.

sections.heading: Check the visible drain path safely
paragraphs: With the washer stopped, look for a kinked drain hose behind the machine and check whether the household standpipe or sink drain is backed up. Do not pull a heavy machine away from the wall if hoses are tight or water is on the floor.

Some front-load models have an owner-accessible pump filter, but many do not. Consult the model manual before opening a filter: trapped water can pour out quickly. If the access point is unclear, leave it for a technician.

sections.heading: When a technician should diagnose the washer
paragraphs: Schedule service if water remains after a model-approved drain cycle, the pump makes an unusual sound, or the problem keeps returning. The drain pump, hose, lid or door lock, and control signals may need testing. A proper diagnosis distinguishes a blockage from a part failure.

When contacting Nova, share the brand and model, any error code, whether the machine is front-load or top-load, and whether the water is still in the tub. We can use those details to plan a washer repair visit in the Austin area.

faq.question: Does a washer that will not drain always need a new pump?
faq.answer: No. A blocked hose or filter, cycle setting, or other control issue can create a similar symptom. The drain path should be checked before replacing the pump.

faq.question: Can I open the pump filter myself?
faq.answer: Only if your owner manual shows an accessible filter and explains how to drain the water safely. Otherwise, a technician should inspect it.

posts.title: Dryer Not Heating? How to Narrow Down the Cause
posts.seoTitle: Dryer Not Heating? Austin Repair Guide
posts.metaDescription: A dryer that tumbles but stays cold may have a power, gas, airflow or heating fault. Learn safe checks and when to book dryer repair in Austin.
posts.excerpt: A turning drum does not prove the heating system works. Start with airflow and basic settings, then arrange a diagnosis if heat is still missing.
posts.imageAlt: Technician inspecting a household clothes dryer in a laundry room

sections.heading: Is the dryer cold or simply slow?
paragraphs: A completely cold dryer and one that gets warm but takes several cycles are different problems. A restricted lint screen or exterior vent can slow drying even when the heater works. A very wet load from a washer spin problem can also make normal drying seem ineffective.

Start by cleaning the lint screen, checking the selected cycle and trying a reasonably sized load. If airflow at the exterior vent seems weak or the vent is blocked, stop using the dryer until the restriction is addressed.

sections.heading: What can interrupt heat production?
paragraphs: Electric dryers can tumble while their heating circuit has a separate power problem. Gas dryers can also tumble when the gas supply or ignition system is not providing heat. Heating elements, thermal fuses, thermostats, igniters and controls require model-specific testing.

Avoid opening electrical or gas compartments to guess at the failed part. A safety device that has operated may be a symptom of another problem, including poor ventilation, so replacing it without finding the cause may not provide a lasting repair.

sections.heading: Information that helps with a repair visit
paragraphs: Tell us whether the dryer is gas or electric, whether the drum turns, whether you feel any heat, and how long a normal load now takes. Share the model number and any recent change to the vent or laundry setup.
Nova diagnoses dryer heating and airflow problems in Austin and nearby communities. We check the relevant systems before explaining the repair and its cost.

faq.question: Why does my dryer turn but not heat?
faq.answer: The motor and heating system can have different causes of failure. Depending on the model, the issue may involve power, gas supply, airflow, a heating component or a control.

faq.question: Can a clogged vent make drying take longer?
faq.answer: Yes. Restricted airflow can extend drying time and should be addressed before continued use.

posts.title: Ice Maker Not Making Ice? Check Water and Temperature First
posts.seoTitle: Ice Maker Not Making Ice? Austin Repair Guide
posts.metaDescription: No ice or slow ice production? Check ice maker settings, freezer temperature, filter and water supply before scheduling ice maker repair in Austin.
posts.excerpt: An ice maker needs the right freezer temperature and water flow. These observations help separate a simple supply issue from a failed assembly.
posts.imageAlt: Technician checking the ice maker compartment inside a refrigerator

sections.heading: Start with the ice maker setting and freezer
paragraphs: First confirm that the ice maker is switched on and that a full bin or raised shutoff arm is not telling it to stop. Controls vary by model, so check the owner manual before changing settings. If the freezer is running warm, ice production can slow or stop even when the ice maker itself is working.

Use a thermometer to compare the actual freezer temperature with the setting. Note whether food is softening or frost is building up; those clues may point to a freezer cooling problem rather than an ice-maker fault.

sections.heading: Look for a water-flow problem
paragraphs: A clogged refrigerator filter, a closed supply valve or a kinked water line can keep the ice maker from filling. If the water dispenser is also slow, that is useful information. Do not force a frozen fill tube or dismantle the water valve without model-specific instructions.
Small or hollow cubes often suggest an incomplete fill, while cubes trapped in the mold suggest a different issue. Reporting the exact pattern helps a technician focus the diagnosis.

sections.heading: When service is the right next step
paragraphs: If the freezer temperature and visible water supply appear normal but ice production does not return, the fill valve, sensors, wiring or ice-maker assembly may need testing. Replacing the assembly before checking water flow can leave the original problem unresolved.

When you contact Nova, send the refrigerator model number, note whether the dispenser works, and describe whether there is no ice, slow ice, leaking or overfilling. We service refrigerator and built-in ice makers across the Austin metro.

faq.question: Can a clogged water filter stop an ice maker?
faq.answer: Yes. Reduced water flow through a clogged filter can prevent proper filling or slow ice production.

faq.question: Does no ice always mean the ice maker assembly failed?
faq.answer: No. Freezer temperature, the on/off setting, water supply, filter and fill valve should also be checked.
